stories.title: Wall Street enters NEAR as a $4 billion-a-month app is hacked
stories.summary: Institutional investors moved into NEAR Protocol. At the same time, a NEAR-based app that handles about $4 billion in monthly volume was hacked. The report does not give the loss size or the attack method.
stories.whyItMatters: A hack on a major app right as institutions arrive tests confidence in NEAR's security at a key moment.
whatToWatch: Official details on the hack's cause and size
Any fix or response from the app's team
Whether institutional interest in NEAR holds up
questions: What caused the hack, and how much was lost?
Will the Wall Street entrants still proceed on NEAR?

sources.title: Wall Street arrived in NEAR just as a $4 billion-a-month app got hacked

stories.title: Bitcoin ETFs near a record inflow month after an 11-month slump
stories.summary: Spot Bitcoin ETFs are about $5 billion short of a new monthly inflow record. This follows an 11-month stretch described as a harsh reset for the funds. The report does not name which ETFs lead the inflows.
stories.whyItMatters: ETF flows are a key gauge of institutional Bitcoin demand, and a record pace would mark a sharp reversal from the recent slump.
whatToWatch: Whether net inflows reach the record in the coming weeks
Which ETF issuers draw the most new money
Bitcoin's price reaction if inflows keep climbing
questions: What drove the 11-month reset in the first place?
Is this inflow pace likely to hold?

sources.title: Bitcoin ETFs are $5 billion away from a new flow record after a brutal 11-month reset

stories.title: MetaMask security scare coincides with a nine-month high in Ethereum validator exits
stories.summary: A security scare tied to the MetaMask wallet lined up with a jump in Ethereum validator exits. Exits are now at their highest level in nine months. The report does not confirm that the scare directly caused the exits, nor does it detail the security issue.
stories.whyItMatters: A wallet scare that lines up with rising validator exits raises questions about confidence in Ethereum's security setup.
whatToWatch: An official MetaMask statement on the issue
Whether validator exits keep rising or reverse
Any confirmed reports of lost funds
questions: What exactly was the MetaMask security issue?
Did the scare cause the exits, or is the timing a coincidence?

sources.title: MetaMask security scare pushes Ethereum validator exits to a nine-month high

stories.title: Rising bond yields revive debate over Bitcoin as a hedge
stories.summary: A sharp rise in bond yields has prompted claims that this favors Bitcoin as a safe-haven asset. The link is a narrative argument, not confirmed by reported capital flows into Bitcoin. Treat the framing of this as Bitcoin's moment with caution.
stories.whyItMatters: The bond-yield-to-Bitcoin argument resurfaces every time rates move, but its track record is mixed, so it deserves skepticism rather than amplification.
whatToWatch: Whether Bitcoin's price actually moves with the yield shift
Further bond market movement in coming days
Any real data on money flowing into Bitcoin
questions: Does past data actually support this correlation?
Who is making this argument, and why?

sources.title: Bond yield explosion gives Bitcoin a strong signal – is now finally Satoshi’s time?

stories.title: Rising US factory costs put pressure on Bitcoin's rally above $85,000
stories.summary: New data shows a spike in US factory input costs. The report says this could threaten Bitcoin's recent rally above $85,000. It does not give the specific index or figures behind the cost spike.
stories.whyItMatters: Signs of rising manufacturing costs can shift interest-rate expectations, and that in turn can move risk assets like Bitcoin.
whatToWatch: Market reaction in the days after this data
Shifts in Federal Reserve rate expectations
Whether Bitcoin holds the $85,000 level
questions: Which specific data release showed the cost spike?
How closely has Bitcoin actually tracked this kind of data lately?

sources.title: US factory costs spike, threatening Bitcoin’s rally above $85,000

stories.title: Senate tax bill eases stablecoin spending, leaves Bitcoin reporting unchanged
stories.summary: A Senate tax bill would ease tax treatment for everyday stablecoin spending. Bitcoin transactions would still need to be reported on IRS forms. The report does not detail the bill's exact terms or its progress through Congress.
stories.whyItMatters: Different tax treatment for stablecoins versus Bitcoin could steer everyday crypto payments toward stablecoins.
whatToWatch: The bill's progress through Senate committees and a floor vote
Any reaction from the House
IRS guidance that may follow passage
questions: Which stablecoin transactions would actually be exempted?
Does the bill have a realistic path to passage?

sources.title: Senate tax bill frees stablecoin spending while Bitcoin stays on IRS forms

stories.title: Treasury to accept state stablecoin applications before finishing its rules
stories.summary: The US Treasury will let states accept applications for stablecoin issuer approval before it finishes the underlying rules. This appears tied to rollout of stablecoin legislation. The report does not name specific states or a timeline for final rules.
stories.whyItMatters: Approvals moving ahead of final rules could speed up stablecoin issuance, but it also creates uncertainty for early applicants.
whatToWatch: Which states open applications first
When Treasury finalizes the rules
Any issuers that gain early approval
questions: What happens to early approvals once final rules are set?
Which states are moving first?

sources.title: Treasury will let states file for stablecoin approval before finishing their rules

stories.title: XRP collateral lending market emerges, dominated by large holders
stories.summary: XRP is starting to be used as collateral for loans, creating a new lending market. The report says large holders, or whales, dominate this early market. It gives no figures on loan volume or rates.
stories.whyItMatters: Collateral use gives XRP a new role beyond trading, but heavy whale concentration adds risk to an early-stage market.
whatToWatch: Growth in the number and size of participants
Whether retail users start to join
Any liquidation events in this market
questions: Who are the whales driving this market?
Which platform or protocol hosts this lending activity?

sources.title: XRP is becoming collateral for real loans and the first market is already dominated by whales

stories.title: UK's planned 2027 crypto rules may block firms from new business with existing customers
stories.summary: The UK's planned 2027 crypto regulatory framework could stop firms from offering new business to their own existing customers under certain conditions. The report does not specify which rule provision causes this or which firms it affects.
stories.whyItMatters: A rule that restricts serving existing customers could disrupt how UK crypto firms operate well before the 2027 deadline.
whatToWatch: Further detail from UK regulators on the rule
Industry pushback or feedback
Possible amendments before the 2027 rollout
questions: Which specific requirement creates this restriction?
Will regulators adjust it after industry feedback?

sources.title: UK’s 2027 crypto rules could block new business with existing customers

stories.title: Open USD bets on Stripe's payment network to challenge USDT and USDC
stories.summary: A new effort called Open USD is betting that Stripe's payment network, said to process $1.9 trillion, can help it compete with the dominant stablecoins USDT and USDC. The report does not detail Open USD's structure, backing, or launch date.
stories.whyItMatters: USDT and USDC dominate stablecoin supply, so a well-connected payments challenger could reshape competition among crypto dollars.
whatToWatch: Launch details and backing for Open USD
Adoption by merchants or platforms
Any shift in USDT and USDC market share
questions: How is Open USD backed and regulated?
What exact role does Stripe play: issuer, distributor, or infrastructure partner?

sources.title: Open USD bets Stripe’s $1.9 trillion network can break USDT and USDC’s grip
